# Civic Chain

> Civic Chain is a municipal procurement and payment transparency platform built on XRPL and RLUSD stablecoin rails. It replaces fragmented contract workflows with a shared ledger that gives town staff, contractors, and residents a live view of every contract dollar — from bid to payout.

## Product

- [Homepage](https://civic-chain.com/): Platform overview, problem statement, how it works, and key statistics.
- [Public Spending Ledger](https://civic-chain.com/citizen): Citizen-facing live contract records and spending data. No login required.
- [Contractor Portal](https://civic-chain.com/vendor): Vendor payment tracking, card activity, and contract status.
- [Contact](https://civic-chain.com/contact): Inquiries for municipalities, counties, school districts, and pilot programs.
- [Roadmap](https://civic-chain.com/roadmap): Planned platform features and development timeline.

## Key Claims

- Vendor payments settle in 4 seconds on XRPL versus 1 to 3 business days on ACH.
- Transaction cost under $0.001 versus $25 to $50 per wire transfer.
- Late payments cost the U.S. construction industry $208 billion in a single year (Rabbet, 2022).
- Roughly 25% of global government procurement spending is lost to inefficiency, approximately $1 trillion per year (World Bank, 2022).
- Built for towns, cities, counties, school districts, HOAs, and any public or quasi-public body that manages shared contractor spend.

## How It Works

1. Municipality publishes a contract request with budget, timeline, and a public starting record.
2. Vendor is awarded the contract. Spend rules and card funding are tied to the contract record on day one.
3. Work is confirmed before payout moves forward. The full record stays visible on a public ledger throughout.

## Technology

- XRP Ledger (XRPL) for 4-second payment settlement at sub-cent transaction cost.
- RLUSD stablecoin for stable-value vendor disbursements.
- Three role-based portals: Town staff, Contractor, and Public.
- Public ledger accessible with no login, no records request, no call to town hall.
